title: EC2 networking troubleshooting playbook
hook: When an EC2 instance cannot be reached, debug outside-in: routing, Network ACLs (NACLs), security groups, ENI placement, then the operating system firewall.

blocks.text: EC2 networking failures stem from layered controls: subnet route tables (Internet Gateway, NAT Gateway, VPC endpoints), stateless NACLs at subnet boundary, stateful security groups on ENIs, Elastic IP versus public IP assignment, and host iptables or Windows firewall. VPC Flow Logs and Reachability Analyzer provide evidence.

entries.plainDefinition: Captures accepted/rejected IP traffic for VPC, subnet, or ENI.
entries.example: REJECT count spikes on NACL deny rule.

entries.plainDefinition: Stateless subnet-level allow/deny rules with numbered priority.
entries.example: Deny inbound 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 at NACL layer.

entries.plainDefinition: Tests whether path between source and destination is allowed.
entries.example: Prove ALB can reach EC2 on port 8080.

entries.plainDefinition: Return traffic uses high ports — NACL must allow ephemeral range.

blocks.text: Random SG edits cause outages. Senior engineers follow a checklist instead of guessing. Same layers apply to Lambda in VPC reaching RDS.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: route table proves path, NACL stateless both directions, SG stateful on ENI, then OS. Use Reachability Analyzer before SSH guessing.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Confirm ENI subnet and IP
items.body: Primary ENI in intended subnet with correct private or public IP.

items.title: Route table
items.body: Public: 0.0.0.0/0 → IGW. Private egress: NAT or endpoints.

items.title: NACL then SG
items.body: NACL inbound/outbound allow required ports and ephemeral return.

items.title: Application listen
items.body: Process bound to 0.0.0.0:port; OS firewall allows; target group port matches.

diagram.title: Troubleshoot layers
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  Client[Client] --> IGW[Internet Gateway]
  IGW --> RT[Route table]
  RT --> NACL[NACL subnet]
  NACL --> SG[Security group ENI]
  SG --> OS[OS firewall + app listen]
  Flow[VPC Flow Logs] -.-> NACL
  Reach[VPC Reachability Analyzer] -.-> SG

snippet.label: VPC Reachability Analyzer path
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-network-insights-path \
  --source ip=10.0.1.5 \
  --destination ip=10.0.10.20,port=8080,protocol=tcp
aws ec2 start-network-insights-analysis \
  --network-insights-path-id nip-0abc
snippet.explanation: Proves whether routing and SG allow path before packet capture.

snippet.label: Enable VPC Flow Logs
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-flow-logs \
  --resource-type NetworkInterface \
  --resource-ids eni-0app \
  --traffic-type REJECT \
  --log-destination-type cloud-watch-logs \
  --log-group-name /vpc/flow/reject
snippet.explanation: Filter REJECT first to find NACL or SG blocks quickly.

snippet.label: Describe SG rules for ENI
snippet.code:
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-0app \
  --query 'NetworkInterfaces[0].Groups'
aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0web
snippet.explanation: SG is stateful — confirm inbound and that return egress is allowed (default allow all egress).

snippet.label: Test from instance with curl and ss
snippet.code:
curl -s --connect-timeout 2 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
ss -tlnp | grep 8080
sudo iptables -L -n
snippet.explanation: On-instance checks: app listening, local firewall, metadata reachable (IMDS).

blocks.title: Runtime and deployment parallels
rows: Wrong HOST env or bind address
No built-in — rely on VPC SG on EC2

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Editing SG without checking NACL ephemeral return. Assuming public IP without IGW route. Debugging SSH when SSM Session Manager is the production access path.

blocks.text: Asymmetric routing breaks NACL return path — common with multi-ENI appliances. How to prove it in production: Flow Logs REJECT reason, Reachability Analyzer failed component, and TargetGroup UnHealthyHostCount correlated with deploy.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Volume and cost at full capture

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Opening SG 0.0.0.0/0 SSH as first fix gets rejected. Strong answer: layered checklist, Reachability Analyzer, SSM access, least privilege SG.

interviewTakeaways: Debug outside-in: route → NACL → SG → OS → application listen port.
NACLs are stateless — allow ephemeral return ports.
VPC Flow Logs and Reachability Analyzer provide evidence, not guesses.
60s: Route IGW/NAT, NACL both ways, SG on ENI, app listens. Flow Logs REJECT. SSM not SSH.
Follow-up: why does NACL block work when SG allows?
commonPitfalls: Fixing only SG when NACL blocks ephemeral return — weak answer.
Strong answer: check NACL inbound and outbound rules with ephemeral port range.
Public IP on instance in private subnet route table — no IGW path.
ALB health check port mismatch with app listen port.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Express app.listen(8080, "0.0.0.0") — binding localhost only breaks ALB health checks, like SG allowing traffic ENI never receives.
/health route must respond before ASG grace expires — similar to k8s readiness probe timing.
